q: Which symptom is a red flag in a child with an anterior mediastinal mass?
why: Also stridor, syncope and SVC obstruction signs.

q: What is the investigation of choice?
why: CT assesses tracheal and vascular compression.

o: Loss of muscle tone can cause complete airway or vascular collapse

q: What should be considered before GA?
o: Whether a tissue diagnosis can be obtained under local, or the mass shrunk with steroids or radiotherapy

q: Airway obstruction occurs on induction. What is an early step?
o: Reposition (lateral, prone or the patient’s preferred position)
why: Then rigid bronchoscopy, or sternotomy to lift the mass if cardiovascular collapse.

q: What is the commonest malignant cause of anterior mediastinal mass in children?
why: Also ALL and germ cell tumours.

q: Which biochemical abnormality is seen in tumour lysis syndrome?
Which drug prevents tumour lysis syndrome?
why: Allopurinol is a xanthine oxidase inhibitor.

q: What line is placed before induction?
why: Rigid bronchoscope and bypass access may also be considered.

q: What is the induction technique classically used?
o: Gas induction maintaining spontaneous ventilation, lateral or head-up
